intro.en: Weight based doses, indications and contraindications of the drugs most often asked in the paediatric practical exam.

items.summary: Everyday fever and pain remedy for children, safe at weight based doses but harmful to the liver in excess.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Brings down raised body temperature in a febrile child.
Eases mild to moderate pain such as headache and body ache.
The book places it with painkiller, antipyretic and anti-inflammatory type medicines.

blocks.title: When to avoid it
bullets: Do not use in a child with liver failure.

blocks.title: Dosage
bullets: 10-15 mg/kg by mouth.
5 mg/kg by the intravenous route (IV).

viva.q: What paracetamol doses does the book quote for a child?
viva.a: 10-15 mg/kg by mouth and 5 mg/kg by vein.

viva.q: Why is paracetamol unsafe once the liver has failed?
viva.a: The liver clears the drug, so a failing liver cannot handle it and injury worsens.

viva.q: Which single dose is larger per kilogram, oral or intravenous?
viva.a: The oral dose of 10-15 mg/kg is larger than the 5 mg/kg vein dose.

items.summary: Penicillin type antibiotic for common coccal infections in children, avoided in kidney failure and penicillin allergy.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Treats infections caused by Gram positive and Gram negative cocci.

blocks.title: Contraindications
bullets: Avoid in a child with kidney (renal) failure.
Avoid in a child known to react to penicillin (hypersensitivity).

blocks.title: Dosage
bullets: 30-50 mg/kg/day by mouth in 3-4 divided doses.
100-300 mg/kg/day by vein in 3-4 divided doses.

viva.q: Which germs does the book list for amoxicillin?
viva.a: Gram positive and Gram negative cocci.

viva.q: Name the two contraindications the book prints.
viva.a: Kidney failure and known penicillin hypersensitivity.

viva.q: Why is the daily amount split into 3-4 doses?
viva.a: Splitting keeps blood levels steady through the day instead of one peak.

items.summary: Older anti-inflammatory drug that the book keeps for acute rheumatic fever, always given with food and never on an empty stomach.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Treats acute rheumatic fever in children.

blocks.title: Points for safe use
bullets: Never give on an empty stomach; give with food or milk.

blocks.title: Dosage
bullets: 90-120 mg/kg/day by mouth, divided every 6 hours.

viva.q: What is the book indication for aspirin in children?
viva.a: Acute rheumatic fever.

viva.q: What stomach advice goes with aspirin?
viva.a: Give it with food, never on an empty stomach.

viva.q: How is the daily dose spaced?
viva.a: 90-120 mg/kg/day by mouth, divided every 6 hours.

unsure: The printed contraindication cell beside aspirin reads only 'Gm-positive' and looks misplaced from another row, so it is left out for the reviewer to check.

items.summary: Broad worm killer used as a single dose for gut worms and as longer courses for tissue parasites and giardia.

groups.label: Gut worms
bullets: Pinworm, roundworm, hookworm and tapeworm infection.
Dwarf tapeworm infection (Hymenolepis nana).

groups.label: Tissue and protozoal infection
bullets: Neurocysticercosis, where pork tapeworm larvae lodge in the brain.

blocks.title: Contraindications
bullets: Avoid when cysts lie inside the eye (ocular cysticercosis).
Avoid when cysts lie inside the brain ventricles (intraventricular cysticercosis).

blocks.title: Dosage
bullets: Under 2 years: 200 mg as a single dose.
Above 2 years: 400 mg as a single dose.
Roundworm infection: repeat the dose after 2 weeks.
Tapeworm, strongyloidosis and dwarf tapeworm: 400 mg once daily for 3 days.
Giardiasis: 400 mg once daily for 5 days.
Neurocysticercosis: 15 mg/kg twice daily for 7 days, starting on the third day of steroid cover.

viva.q: What single dose treats worms above 2 years of age?
viva.a: 400 mg once; under 2 years it is 200 mg once.

viva.q: When is the dose repeated in roundworm infection?
viva.a: Repeat one dose after 2 weeks.

viva.q: Why is albendazole withheld in ocular cysticercosis?
viva.a: Killing cysts inside the eye can inflame and damage vision.

items.summary: Main drug for filarial infection and tropical eosinophilia, given in three divided doses a day for three weeks.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Treats filariasis.
Treats tropical eosinophilia.

blocks.title: Dosage
bullets: Filariasis: 6 mg/kg/day in doses every 8 hours for 3 weeks.
Tropical eosinophilia: 10 mg/kg/day in doses every 8 hours for 3 weeks.

viva.q: Name the two book indications for DEC.
viva.a: Filariasis and tropical eosinophilia.

viva.q: How are the daily doses spaced and for how long?
viva.a: Every 8 hours for 3 weeks.

viva.q: How does the filariasis dose differ from tropical eosinophilia?
viva.a: Filariasis takes 6 mg/kg/day; tropical eosinophilia takes 10 mg/kg/day.

unsure: The book prints no contraindication row for DEC, so none is listed here.

items.summary: Injectable antibiotic reserved for serious Gram negative infections, never given to a child with myasthenia gravis.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Treats Gram negative bacterial infections.

blocks.title: Contraindications
bullets: Avoid in a child with myasthenia gravis.

blocks.title: Dosage
bullets: 5-7.5 mg/kg/day into vein or muscle (intravenous or intramuscular), twice daily.

viva.q: Which infections does the book list for gentamicin?
viva.a: Gram negative infections.

viva.q: Why is it withheld in myasthenia gravis?
viva.a: It can worsen the muscle weakness of that disease.

viva.q: What is the daily dose and route?
viva.a: 5-7.5 mg/kg/day by vein or muscle, twice daily.

items.summary: Cephalosporin antibiotic given by mouth for respiratory, urinary, dysentery and enteric fever in children.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Upper respiratory tract infection (URTI).
Urinary tract infection (UTI).
Acute bacillary dysentery.
Enteric (typhoid type) fever.

blocks.title: Contraindications
bullets: Avoid after penicillin or cephalosporin allergy (hypersensitivity).

blocks.title: Dosage
bullets: Usual dose: 10 mg/kg/day by mouth, twice daily.
Enteric fever: 20 mg/kg/day by mouth, twice daily.

viva.q: List the four book indications for cefixime.
viva.a: URTI, UTI, acute bacillary dysentery and enteric fever.

viva.q: Who should not receive it?
viva.a: A child with penicillin or cephalosporin hypersensitivity.

viva.q: How does the enteric fever dose differ?
viva.a: It doubles to 20 mg/kg/day, still twice daily by mouth.

items.summary: Injectable cephalosporin listed for the same respiratory, urinary, gut and enteric fever indications as cefixime.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Upper respiratory tract infection (URTI).
Urinary tract infection (UTI).
Acute bacillary dysentery.
Enteric (typhoid type) fever.

blocks.title: Contraindications
bullets: Avoid after penicillin or cephalosporin allergy (hypersensitivity).

blocks.title: Dosage
bullets: 50-100 mg/kg/day by vein, once or twice daily.

viva.q: How is ceftriaxone given, and at what dose?
viva.a: By vein, 50-100 mg/kg/day once or twice daily.

viva.q: Which allergy bars its use?
viva.a: Penicillin or cephalosporin hypersensitivity.

viva.q: How does it differ from cefixime in route?
viva.a: Ceftriaxone goes by vein; cefixime goes by mouth.

unsure: The printed table merges one indication cell across cefixime and ceftriaxone; the four indications are repeated here for the reviewer to confirm.

items.summary: Short course oral antibiotic that the book lists for atypical pneumonia in children.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Treats atypical pneumonia.

blocks.title: Contraindications
bullets: Avoid under 6 weeks of age, as printed in the book.

blocks.title: Dosage
bullets: 10 mg/kg/day by mouth, once daily for 3 days.

viva.q: What is the book indication for azithromycin?
viva.a: Atypical pneumonia.

viva.q: What dose and duration does the book give?
viva.a: 10 mg/kg/day by mouth for 3 days.

viva.q: Which age bar does the book print?
viva.a: Under 6 weeks of age.

items.summary: First line rescue drug that stops status epilepticus and febrile seizures, given by vein, mouth or rectum.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Stops status epilepticus (a seizure that will not end on its own).
Treats febrile seizures in young children.

blocks.title: Contraindications
bullets: Avoid in myasthenia gravis.
Avoid in acute narrow angle glaucoma.

blocks.title: Dosage
bullets: 0.3-0.5 mg/kg/dose by vein, mouth or rectum (intravenous, oral or per rectal).

viva.q: When is diazepam the rescue drug?
viva.a: Status epilepticus and febrile seizures.

viva.q: Name its two printed contraindications.
viva.a: Myasthenia gravis and acute narrow angle glaucoma.

viva.q: What dose and routes does the book quote?
viva.a: 0.3-0.5 mg/kg/dose by vein, mouth or rectum.

items.summary: Daily antiepileptic for partial and tonic clonic seizures, also listed for post herpetic nerve pain.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Treats partial tonic clonic seizures.
Eases post herpetic neuralgia (nerve pain after shingles).

blocks.title: Contraindications
bullets: Avoid in a child taking MAOI drugs (monoamine oxidase inhibitors).
Avoid in porphyria (a disorder of haem pigment handling).

blocks.title: Dosage
bullets: 10-30 mg/kg/day by mouth, twice or three times daily.

viva.q: Which seizures does carbamazepine cover in the book?
viva.a: Partial tonic clonic seizures.

viva.q: What non seizure use is printed?
viva.a: Post herpetic neuralgia.

viva.q: What blocks its use?
viva.a: MAOI drugs and porphyria.

items.summary: Older barbiturate antiepileptic valued for neonatal seizures and for preventing febrile seizures, started with a loading dose.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Treats neonatal seizures.
Treats tonic clonic seizures.
Prevents febrile seizures (prophylaxis).

blocks.title: Contraindications
bullets: Avoid in porphyria.
Avoid in liver and kidney disease.

blocks.title: Dosage
bullets: Loading dose: 20 mg/kg.
Maintenance: 5 mg/kg/day, once or twice daily.

viva.q: Which seizure setting is phenobarbitone known for?
viva.a: Neonatal seizures and febrile seizure prophylaxis.

viva.q: What loading and maintenance doses are printed?
viva.a: 20 mg/kg loading, then 5 mg/kg/day once or twice daily.

viva.q: When is it contraindicated?
viva.a: In porphyria and in liver or kidney disease.

items.summary: Daily antiepileptic for generalised and tonic clonic seizures and for trigeminal nerve pain, using the same loading schedule as phenobarbitone.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Treats tonic clonic and generalised seizures.
Eases trigeminal neuralgia (face nerve pain).

blocks.title: Contraindications
bullets: Avoid in porphyria.
Avoid in heart block.

blocks.title: Dosage
bullets: Loading dose: 20 mg/kg.
Maintenance: 5 mg/kg/day, once or twice daily.

viva.q: Which seizures does the book list for phenytoin?
viva.a: Tonic clonic and generalised seizures.

viva.q: What pain use is printed?
viva.a: Trigeminal neuralgia.

viva.q: How does its schedule compare with phenobarbitone?
viva.a: Identical: 20 mg/kg loading, then 5 mg/kg/day.

items.summary: Broad spectrum antiepileptic that covers most childhood epilepsies, but must be avoided in liver disease.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Broad cover for the majority of epilepsies in children.

blocks.title: Contraindications
bullets: Avoid in liver (hepatic) disease.

blocks.title: Dosage
bullets: 10-60 mg/kg/day, twice or three times daily.

viva.q: Why is valproate called broad spectrum?
viva.a: It covers the majority of childhood epilepsies.

viva.q: What is its key contraindication?
viva.a: Liver disease.

viva.q: What daily range does the book quote?
viva.a: 10-60 mg/kg/day, twice or three times daily.

items.summary: Prokinetic antiemetic for reflux oesophagitis and acute vomiting, unsafe with gut bleeding or raised prolactin states.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Treats reflux oesophagitis (acid washing back into the food pipe).
Treats acute nausea and vomiting.

blocks.title: Contraindications
bullets: Avoid with raised prolactin (prolactinaemia).
Avoid with bleeding from the gut (gastrointestinal haemorrhage).

blocks.title: Dosage
bullets: 0.2-0.4 mg/kg/dose.

viva.q: What gut uses does the book list for domperidone?
viva.a: Reflux oesophagitis and acute nausea with vomiting.

viva.q: When is it contraindicated?
viva.a: With raised prolactin and with gut bleeding.

viva.q: What dose is quoted?
viva.a: 0.2-0.4 mg/kg per dose.

items.summary: Revised DOTS chart sorting new and previously treated children into Category I and II with their intensive and continuation phases.

blocks.title: Reading the code
blocks.text: H, R, Z, E and S stand for isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, ethambutol and streptomycin. The leading number counts months and the subscript counts doses each week.

head: Treatment group
Type of patient
Intensive phase
Continuation phase
rows: New sputum smear positive, new smear negative, new extrapulmonary, new others
Smear positive relapse, failure, defaulter after treatment, others

blocks.title: Weight based doses of each drug
bullets: Isoniazid (H): 10 mg/kg.
Rifampicin (R): 15 mg/kg.
Pyrazinamide (Z): 35 mg/kg.
Ethambutol (E): 35 mg/kg.
Streptomycin (S): 15-20 mg/kg.

viva.q: How long is the intensive phase for a new case?
viva.a: 2 months of H3R3Z3E3, then 4 months of H3R3.

viva.q: What extra drugs does Category II add?
viva.a: Streptomycin in intensive phase and ethambutol in continuation.

viva.q: What are the per kilogram doses of H, R, Z and E?
viva.a: H 10, R 15, Z 35 and E 35 mg/kg.

title.en: Chloroquine for malaria in low resistance areas

items.summary: Chloroquine schedules for areas where resistance is unlikely and the species is not falciparum, with doses counted in base drug.

blocks.title: Counting the dose
blocks.text: Doses below are counted as base drug. One 250 mg chloroquine tablet holds 150 mg of base. The total course is 25 mg base/kg spread over 3 days taken by mouth.

groups.label: WHO schedule
bullets: 10 mg base/kg at once, then 5 mg base/kg after 6 hours, after 24 hours and after 48 hours.

groups.label: National programme schedule
bullets: 10 mg base/kg at once, then 10 mg base/kg after 24 hours and 5 mg base/kg after 48 hours.

blocks.title: Primaquine to stop vivax relapse
bullets: One 15 mg tablet holds 15 mg of base primaquine.
Plasmodium vivax: 0.25 mg base/kg daily for 14 days.

viva.q: How much base sits in a 250 mg chloroquine tablet?
viva.a: 150 mg of base.

viva.q: How does the WHO course differ from the national one?
viva.a: WHO gives 10 then 5, 5, 5 mg/kg; national gives 10 then 10, 5 mg/kg.

viva.q: Why is primaquine added for vivax malaria?
viva.a: To prevent relapse: 0.25 mg base/kg daily for 14 days.

title.en: Falciparum and mixed malaria: ACT treatment

items.summary: Artemisinin combination therapy for chloroquine resistant falciparum malaria in India, with single dose partners and a longer primaquine tail for mixed infection.

blocks.title: When ACT is needed
blocks.text: Plasmodium falciparum in India counts as chloroquine resistant, so the book advises ACT (artemisinin combination therapy) built on artesunate 50 mg tablets.

blocks.title: Single dose partner drugs
bullets: Sulphadoxine with pyrimethamine: single dose on day 1 at 1.25 mg/kg from a 500 mg plus 25 mg tablet.
Primaquine: single dose on day 2 at 0.25 mg base/kg from a 7.5 mg or 15 mg tablet.

blocks.title: Mixed infection
bullets: Give ACT together with primaquine 0.25 mg base/kg once daily for 14 days.

viva.q: Why does falciparum malaria in India need ACT?
viva.a: It is chloroquine resistant, so artemisinin combination therapy is used.

viva.q: What partner doses does the book print?
viva.a: Sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine 1.25 mg/kg on day 1; primaquine 0.25 mg base/kg on day 2.

viva.q: How is mixed infection handled?
viva.a: ACT plus primaquine 0.25 mg base/kg daily for 14 days.

unsure: The artesunate weight band rows (14, 24 and 34 mg/kg across day 1 to 3) are jumbled in print and are left out; the tablet strength line for the sulphadoxine combination is also unclear.

items.summary: Rapid fire antidote chart pairing seventeen common poisons with their specific reversals for the practical exam.

blocks.title: How to use this chart
blocks.text: Read the poison on the left and its antidote on the right. Examiners fire single pairs, so learn each pair both ways round.

groups.label: Painkillers and brain drugs
bullets: Paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose: give N-acetyl cysteine.
Amphetamine poisoning: give chlorpromazine.
Morphine and opioid poisoning: give naloxone.
Benzodiazepine (diazepam) poisoning: give flumazenil.
Isoniazid poisoning: give pyridoxine (vitamin B6).

groups.label: Cholinergic, clotting and bite poisons
bullets: Atropine or belladonna poisoning: give physostigmine.
Organophosphorus (OP) poisoning: give atropine.
Heparin excess: give protamine sulfate.
Warfarin excess: give vitamin K.
Scorpion sting: give prazosin.

groups.label: Gases, metals and blood poisons
bullets: Carbon dioxide narcosis: give oxygen.
Cyanide poisoning: give amyl nitrite.
Ethylene glycol poisoning: give ethanol.
Mercury or lead poisoning: give BAL (British anti-Lewisite, dimercaprol).
Arsenic poisoning: give EDTA (ethylenediaminetetra-acetic acid).
Iron poisoning: give desferoxamine.
Methaemoglobinaemia: give methylene blue.

viva.q: What reverses paracetamol and morphine poisoning?
viva.a: N-acetyl cysteine for paracetamol, naloxone for morphine.

viva.q: Atropine treats one poisoning but causes another: explain.
viva.a: Atropine reverses OP poisoning, while atropine poisoning itself needs physostigmine.

viva.q: What reverses heparin, warfarin and iron?
viva.a: Protamine sulfate, vitamin K and desferoxamine respectively.

title.en: Emergency drugs for arrest and unstable rhythms

items.summary: Four resuscitation drugs every student must quote by heart: adrenaline, atropine, adenosine and amiodarone with their exact paediatric doses.

blocks.title: Drug, indication and dose
bullets: Adrenaline (epinephrine) for bradycardia, asystole and pulseless arrest: 0.1 ml/kg/dose of 1:10000, repeatable after 3 minutes by vein.
Atropine for bradycardia from heart block (atrioventricular block): 0.02 mg/kg/dose by vein.
Adenosine for supraventricular tachycardia: 0.1 mg/kg by vein, repeatable at 0.2 mg/kg after 2 minutes.
Amiodarone for ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation: 5 mg/kg by vein.

viva.q: What adrenaline dose is used in pulseless arrest?
viva.a: 0.1 ml/kg of 1:10000 by vein, repeated after 3 minutes.

viva.q: When is atropine preferred over adrenaline?
viva.a: In bradycardia caused by primary heart block: 0.02 mg/kg by vein.

viva.q: How is adenosine dosed for SVT?
viva.a: 0.1 mg/kg by vein, repeated at 0.2 mg/kg after 2 minutes.

viva.q: Which drug covers ventricular tachycardia and fibrillation?
viva.a: Amiodarone 5 mg/kg by vein.

items.summary: Two correction drugs for acidosis and potassium or calcium emergencies, with the slow push rule for calcium.

blocks.title: Drug, indication and dose
bullets: Sodium bicarbonate for metabolic acidosis and high potassium (hyperkalaemia): 1-2 mEq/kg as an intravenous bolus.
Calcium gluconate 10 percent for low calcium (hypocalcaemia) and high potassium: 1 ml/kg given slowly by vein.

viva.q: When is sodium bicarbonate given, and at what dose?
viva.a: In metabolic acidosis and hyperkalaemia: 1-2 mEq/kg IV bolus.

viva.q: What are the two indications for calcium gluconate?
viva.a: Hypocalcaemia and hyperkalaemia.

viva.q: How fast is calcium gluconate pushed?
viva.a: Slowly by vein: 1 ml/kg of the 10 percent solution.

items.summary: What to order and what rise to expect: packed cells, fresh frozen plasma, platelets and cryoprecipitate in children.

blocks.title: Products, triggers and expected rise
bullets: Packed red cells: 10-15 ml/kg of cross matched blood or O negative blood.
One unit of packed cells lifts haemoglobin by about 3 gm%.
Fresh frozen plasma (FFP): 10 ml/kg.
Platelet concentrate: one unit for every 10 kg of body weight.
One platelet unit lifts the count by 20000-50000 per cubic mm.
Cryoprecipitate is rich in factor VIII, von Willebrand factor and fibrinogen.

viva.q: How much packed cells do you order per kilogram?
viva.a: 10-15 ml/kg of cross matched or O negative blood.

viva.q: What haemoglobin rise follows one unit?
viva.a: About 3 gm%.

viva.q: How are platelets dosed and what rise follows?
viva.a: One unit per 10 kg; the count rises 20000-50000 per cubic mm.
